mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota Yaris 1.0 or 1.3 VVT-i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used Toyota Yaris 1.0 VVT-i (1KR-FE) engine costs £300-£700 supply-only; reconditioned units are £900-£1,800; fully rebuilt engines range from £1,500-£2,800 supply-only [EM-QUOTE]. For the 1.3 VVT-i (2NZ-FE, 2SZ-FE), used units cost £350-£800; reconditioned are £1,000-£2,000; rebuilt range from £1,800-£3,000. Fitting adds approximately £390-£520 in labour at an independent specialist (6-8 hours).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of VVT-i failure in a Toyota Yaris?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common symptom is the check engine light accompanied by code P0011 (1KR-FE) or P1349 (2NZ-FE), followed by rough idling, loss of power and poor fuel economy. You may notice the engine struggling to accelerate or running unevenly at low speeds.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Yaris 1.0 or 1.3 VVT-i?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Toyota Yaris 1.0 or 1.3 VVT-i (2005-2015) is worth approximately £1,500-£6,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. A reconditioned or rebuilt engine at £900-£3,000 supply-only represents 20-60% of the vehicle's value - which can be viable, especially if the car is otherwise well-maintained and has low mileage.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Toyota Yaris 1.0 VVT-i (1KR-FE) and the earlier 1.0 (1SZ-FE)?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1KR-FE is a 3-cylinder engine introduced in 2005 for the Mk2 Yaris, replacing the 4-cylinder 1SZ-FE from the Mk1. The 1KR-FE produces 68-69hp and is lighter and more fuel-efficient than its predecessor. The 1SZ-FE (1999-2005) produced 68hp from a 4-cylinder configuration.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota Yaris VVT-i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional engine replacement on a Toyota Yaris 1.0 or 1.3 VVT-i typically takes 6-8 working hours for an experienced specialist. Allow 2-3 working days from workshop drop-off to collection, depending on parts availability and workshop workload.

mainEntity.name: How reliable is the Toyota Yaris 1.0 and 1.3 VVT-i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Toyota Yaris 1.0 and 1.3 VVT-i engines are among the most reliable small petrol engines on the market, with many examples exceeding 150,000 miles. The 1KR-FE three-cylinder and 2NZ-FE/2SZ-FE four-cylinder units are known for their durability and low running costs.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota Yaris 1.0 / 1.3 VVT-i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Toyota Yaris 1.0 and 1.3 VVT-i petrol engines have powered Britain's favourite supermini across three generations since 1999. From the original 1SZ-FE and 2SZ-FE units through to the later 1KR-FE three-cylinder and 1NR-FE Dual VVT-i, these engines are known for their durability, low running costs and straightforward maintenance - making them a popular choice for UK city drivers, first-time buyers and budget-conscious motorists.

milestones.description: **1999** - XP10 Yaris launched with 1.0L 1SZ-FE (4-cylinder, 68hp) and 1.3L 2NZ-FE (4-cylinder, 86hp) VVT-i petrol engines
**2006** - 1.3L 2SZ-FE continues; 1.4L D-4D diesel (1ND-TV) joins the range
**2009** - 1.33L 1NR-FE Dual VVT-i (100hp) introduced for Mk2 facelift and Mk3 models
**2011** - XP130 (Mk3) Yaris launched; 1.0L 1KR-FE and 1.33L 1NR-FE remain core petrol options
**2020** - Mk4 Yaris launched with new Dynamic Force engines; 1KR-FE and 1NR-FE phased out in UK

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Toyota Yaris 1.0 and 1.3 VVT-i range is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Toyota Yaris 1.0 / 1.3 VVT-i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Toyota Yaris 1.0 and 1.3 VVT-i engines (1KR-FE, 2NZ-FE, 2SZ-FE, 1NR-FE) are generally among the most reliable small petrol engines on UK roads. However, the VVT-i system - the engine's defining feature - is also its most common failure point. Rebuilt Yaris VVT-i engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: VVT-i System Failure - Why the Toyota Yaris 1.0 VVT-i 1KR-FE Loses Power
problems.rootCause: The VVT-i camshaft timer (oil control valve) can fail, causing the ECU to detect a mismatch between requested and actual camshaft timing - triggering code P0011 and resulting in rough idling, reduced power and poor fuel economy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace camshaft timer / oil control valve only
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; engine otherwise healthy
Best if other issues present or high mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Toyota Yaris 1.0 or 1.3 VVT-i (2005-2015) is worth approximately £1,500-£6,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. If your Yaris is worth under ~£2,000, a used engine or VVT-i controller-only repair typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. For vehicles worth £2,000-£4,000, evaluate both options; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. For vehicles worth £4,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability.
problems.recommendation: If your Toyota Yaris VVT-i has triggered a VVT-i-related error code (P0011, P1349) and is otherwise healthy, the controller-only repair at an independent specialist offers the best value - often under £500 fitted. If the engine has high mileage (over 100,000 miles) or exhibits other symptoms like oil consumption or timing chain noise, a full replacement with a reconditioned or rebuilt unit is the more cost-effective long-term decision.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 1KR-FE Toyota Yaris 1.0 VVT-i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Timing Chain Wear - Long-Term Reliability Concerns
problems.rootCause: The 2NZ-FE and 2SZ-FE engines can develop oil consumption issues and timing chain stretch over time, leading to cold-start rattles, cam/crank correlation codes and rough running.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; engine otherwise healthy
Best for high-mileage engines with multiple issues

problems.recommendation: The 2NZ-FE is a non-interference engine, meaning a broken timing chain won't destroy the valves - but it will leave you stranded. If you hear cold-start rattle or have cam/crank correlation codes, have the chain inspected immediately. For high-mileage Yaris 1.3 VVT-i examples (over 120,000 miles), a full replacement with a reconditioned engine often makes more sense than investing in piecemeal repairs.
